page: Vultr vx1-g-192c-768g is a virtual server instance within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features 192 dedicated vCPUs powered by AMD x86_64 processors, paired with 768.0 GB of system memory. This configuration establishes a balanced resource distribution of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The instance does not include any local GPU hardware, limiting its applicability for hardware-accelerated graphics or direct GPU-based machine learning workloads. Local storage is restricted to a nominal 1 GB network-backed volume, indicating that primary data storage must be provisioned via external network-attached storage volumes. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is included with the instance.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the vx1-g-192c-768g offers high resource density for workloads requiring massive parallel CPU execution without the overhead of local physical storage. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing capabilities. This profile is suitable for large-scale general-purpose workloads, highly parallelized CPU tasks, distributed memory caching, and applications utilizing external network storage architectures.
